text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (13.5%, 3.8%, 10.77, z 1.67, 24%, 30 docs, 3 of 22) and the leaning is appropriately cautious. But the narrative has factual and quality flaws: a leaked internal note about a non-existent claim, a claim of 'every complexity tier' that the card does not support as stated, and wording inconsistent with the data. An investigator would need to clean up and re-verify some points.","problems":["Rationale contains leaked drafting text: 'C0049590 is not in the packet so is excluded', which is unprofessional and signals unreliable grounding.","Cited examples include claims whose diagnoses do not match the stated descriptions: it claims 'rash' among low-complexity diagnoses, but no rash dx appears in the packet (R21 is rash, but only coded, not labelled); C0049421 is N39.0 UTI, fine, but the description relies on unlabeled codes.","Headline says 'above expectation in every complexity tier' while the card compares to all-provider share, not risk-adjusted expectation per tier; slight mismatch in framing.","Claim that the overall mix is 'heavily concentrated at 99214' is irrelevant to upcoding to 99215 and is not tied to any number (1420 of 2010 = 71%) in the text.","Statement that all documented 99213/99214 claims support billed level is backed only by 27 claims, and the 99215 sample is only 3, which the summary does acknowledge, but the sampled-chart selection method is not flagged as potentially non-random.","Next steps are generic: they ask for a larger sample of 99214 and 99215 but the rationale recommends targeting low-complexity 99215 claims; the code-written steps do not name the specific claims, so they are inconsistent with the rationale.","The data-reviewed signal (3 of 22 with no lab on claim) is speculative ('cloned templates') and weakly supported.","Cited_claim_ids lists only two claims although many more are cited in the text."]}
